en: Paṭisambhidāmagga 3:
Paññāvagga 3.5.
Discourse on Conduct (Cariyākathā)
"Conduct" (*cariyā*) refers to eight types of conduct:

conduct of posture (*iriyāpatha-cariyā*), conduct of the sense bases (*āyatana-cariyā*), conduct of mindfulness (*sati-cariyā*), conduct of concentration (*samādhi-cariyā*), conduct of knowledge (*ñāṇa-cariyā*), conduct of the path (*magga-cariyā*), conduct of attainment (*patti-cariyā*), and conduct for the welfare of the world (*lokattha-cariyā*).
"Conduct of posture" refers to the four postures.
The practice of the sense bases refers to the six internal and external sense bases.
The practice of mindfulness refers to the four foundations of mindfulness.
The practice of concentration refers to the four jhānas.
The conduct of knowledge refers to the four noble truths.
The conduct of the path refers to the four noble paths.
The conduct of attainment refers to the four fruits of recluseship.
The practice for the welfare of the world pertains to the Tathāgatas, the Arahants, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones; in part, to the Paccekabuddhas; and in part, to the disciples.
The practice of postures pertains to those who have fulfilled their aspirations.
The practice of the sense bases pertains to those who guard the doors of the faculties.
The practice of mindfulness for those who dwell in heedfulness;
the practice of concentration for those devoted to higher mental training;
and the practice of knowledge for those endowed with wisdom.
The practice of the path for those who have entered upon the right way;
the practice of attainment for those who have realized the fruit;
and the practice for the welfare of the world by the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones, as well as by Paccekabuddhas and disciples.
These are the eight modes of conduct.
There are another eight modes of conduct:
one who resolves conducts with faith; one who exerts conducts with energy; one who establishes conducts with mindfulness;
One who practices non-distraction courses by means of concentration; one who understands courses by means of wisdom; one who discerns courses by means of consciousness;
one who courses by way of the "bringing-in" (āyatana) practice, thinking, "For one practicing thus, wholesome states are brought in";
and one who courses by way of the "distinction" (visesa) practice, thinking, "One practicing thus attains distinction."
These are the eight modes of conduct.
There are another eight modes of conduct:
the mode of conduct of seeing, which is right view; the mode of conduct of directing, which is right intention; and the mode of conduct of embracing...
And there is the conduct of right speech; the conduct of origination for right action; the conduct of purification for right livelihood;
the conduct of exertion for right effort; the conduct of establishment for right mindfulness; and the conduct of non-distraction for right concentration.
These are the eight types of conduct.
The Discourse on Conduct is finished.
